added.name: horizontal.
added.long_description:
Every factory will be run by AI agents. Horizontal is building them.

Today, the work that keeps production moving is scattered across people, teams, and disconnected software. When plans change, materials run short, or quality issues appear, factory teams piece together the context and coordinate the response by hand.

Horizontal's AI agents take on that operational work inside the systems factories already use. They replan production around a disruption, investigate quality issues and coordinate order releases across teams and tools. Manufacturers start with one process and add agents over time, building toward a system that coordinates the factory end to end.

Factories are demanding environments for AI: every plant has its own systems and procedures, and every action must work in the context of real production. Our team combines mechanical engineering and shop-floor experience with a track record of building and deploying agentic AI in global industrial companies.

Horizontal connects the people, software and machines that run production.
added.one_liner: AI agents that run factory operations end-to-end.

added.name: Spacesheep

Agents now write faster than anyone can read. Spacesheep is where their work lands: any agent turns a session's output into a space that your team takes in at a glance. It works with the agents you already use, and has its own agent built in.

Teams work on it together: comment on the exact spot, @mention a teammate, or ask @spacesheep and an agent makes the change live on every screen. Every change is a version, and every space is searchable by meaning, for people and agents alike. Spaces can show live data streamed from servers and sensors, and connect to the tools your team already uses.

Teams use it for research, design docs, dashboards, slides and internal apps.

We’re building AI-powered systems that automate manual work in scientific labs using robotics.

Scientists simply type their experiment in plain English. Zeon translates it into code and runs it on robotic arms (no coding required).

By controlling robots with natural language, we’re enabling automation for every lab, every scientist, and every experiment.

Zeon is lab-aware. It detects equipment, adapts to protocols, and moves autonomously between instruments to execute full workflows.

We’re already working with labs at Stanford and UCSF to accelerate discovery - from running overnight nanoparticle fluorescence measurements to safely disposing of hundreds of bacterial samples. 

Zeon reclaims time for what matters most: the science.

long_description.before: Skillsync gives you one place for everything your agents have ever done, and makes all of it portable. Move a full session between Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and any other agent with nothing lost, including the entire conversation, the model's reasoning, and every tool call, not just a summary, so the next agent picks up like it was there the whole time. Because your sessions are portable, they stack up instead of disappearing. Every past session stays searchable and feeds your next agent automatically, so you never re-explain yourself or redo work you have already done. Everything stays on your machine and nothing leaves unless you choose to send it. Skillsync is local-first and yours, and its core engine, txcript, is open source, a portable session format that no single provider owns.

long_description.before:
Sparkles is like Lovable for existing projects, so even Sharon from Marketing can change the button styling on the front page without going back and forth with the dev team.

Someone technical connects their GitHub to Sparkles, sets up the repository and environment variables, and then anyone on the team with a @yourcompany.com email can log in on Sparkles and create pull requests without needing to know what Git is.
long_description.after:
Sparkles gives your whole team coding agents that work on your real codebase.

Connect your GitHub repos once, and anyone on the team can start a run from the web app or by @mentioning Sparkles in Slack. Pick Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode and describe the change in plain language. The agent works in an isolated cloud sandbox with your tools already plugged in, like Linear, Sentry, Notion and Figma. You can watch every command and file edit live and jump in mid-run.

Every run ends as a GitHub pull request. CI checks stream back into Sparkles, and your reviews and branch protections still apply, so prod stays safe.

long_description.before:
58% of the $400B call center industry runs on on-prem phone systems, and until now bringing AI voice automation to them meant ripping out their entire infrastructure first. That's the largest unserved segment in the market. Callab AI connects directly to legacy PBX systems like Avaya, Cisco UCM, and Mitel, and automates up to 70% of call volume with zero migration needed.

We plug into these environments without requiring a rip-and-replace. We serve clients across three continents, including brands like Dunkin Donuts.
long_description.after:
Callab AI is a human-centered customer engagement platform for enterprise contact centers. It lets teams deploy AI agents that handle inbound and outbound conversations across voice, chat, and messaging, while human agents and supervisors stay in control of every interaction.

The platform has two sides. The AI side lets teams build, deploy, and evaluate voice and text agents using a shared knowledge base, embedded evaluations, post-call analysis, data extraction, batch calling, and call transfer. The human side provides a dialer and a live supervision dashboard, from which a person can watch any AI conversation in real time, step in, and hand it back without the customer repeating a word.

Every agent retains memory across channels, so a customer who called yesterday and writes today is recognized and picked up where they left off. The system learns from each human intervention and improves in the direction the team chooses.

Callab AI runs on its own carrier-grade telephony stack and connects natively to Cisco, Mitel, Avaya, SIP trunks, and on-premises PBX systems. Enterprises can adopt it without migrating to the cloud first. The platform maintains SOC 2 controls and serves customers in financial services, healthcare, hospitality, and retail.

Key features:

- AI voice and text agents: Agents handle inbound and outbound conversations across phone, chat, and messaging from a single configuration.

- Live human supervision: Supervisors watch any AI conversation in real time and take over without the customer repeating a word.

- Persistent memory: Every customer's full context is retained across channels and over time.

- AI builder: Teams design, test, and deploy agents without engineering support.

- Embedded evaluations: Every conversation is scored continuously, so performance is measured rather than assumed.

- Self-improving agents: Agents learn from human interventions and get better with every conversation.

- Post-call analysis and data extraction: Every conversation becomes structured, searchable records.

- Batch calling and call transfer: Outbound campaigns run at scale, and conversations move to a human with full context attached.

- Native telephony integration: The platform connects directly to Cisco, Mitel, Avaya, SIP trunks, and on-premises PBX without cloud migration.

- SOC 2 controls: Security and compliance support deployments in regulated industries.

Callab AI delivers every agent production-ready. Our team studies the customer's workflows, internal processes, and existing systems, then builds, tests, and implements the agent on that foundation, so it performs to the organization's own standard from the first live conversation.

We research complex, high-fidelity simulations for training and evaluating frontier AI models, alongside the infrastructure to test and deploy them at scale. Our research focuses on simulations with realistic socialization, multi-agent interaction, swarms, and ultra-long-horizon tasks.

Try one of our first releases, Multi-Agent Arena (https://olamarena.com/), where humans come play social strategy games against multiple AI agents. It has multi-agent social games like Poker, Diplomacy, Risk, and more.
long_description.after:
We push the complexity of simulations in order to provide labs with better model training and evaluations for their capability and safety needs. We achieve this through methods like multi-agent interaction and swarm RL.

We also run olamarena.com where humans come play multi-agent social games against models and inform our public evaluations on human <> agent interaction.

long_description.before:
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI agents faster and keep them secure in production.

Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Armorer's detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks. Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won't feel the delay.

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS, including its first customer-facing AI security agent, which scaled to 100k+ customers. Armorer is backed by Paul Vixie, Internet Hall of Fame inductee and former AWS Deputy CISO.
